Concept: Promoting Information Integrity and Resilience Initiative (PRO-INFO)
I. Problem Statement
Mis/dis/malinformation has become one of the most enduring challenges of our time, affecting
democracy in the Global North and South. We are at a watershed moment in how we respond to
the threat of disinformation. If we do not come together as a community of democracies to shape
the enabling environment that best responds to disinformation and toaddress whole-of-society
approaches that put information integrity and resilience at the forefront of our strategies around
democratic renewal, we will lose the moment to ensure a human rights centered approach to
governance.
The problems center around four main issues. First, while current bilateral and multilateral fora
have made initial investments to address information integrity and resilience, no platform exists
to bring together countries from Global North and South along with stakeholders from the
private sector, content producers, civil society, and emerging technology companies to jointly
address this challenge. Similarly, no donor coordination platform has the ability to rally
development agencies to spur investment for this critical challenge and agree on how to develop
and implement responses that effectively respond to the issue. Third, greater investment is
needed at the country level to strengthen capacity building efforts and bring diverse stakeholders
to the table to respond to disinformation related challenges with appropriate localized context.
Fourth, gender-based disinformation, including disinformation and propaganda aimed at women,
Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trangender, Queer, Plus (LGBTQ+), immigrants/minority populations
and other marginalized groups, is a growing problem that undermines democratic principles and
values, drives a wedge between citizens, and fosters stigmatization.
II. Objectives, Key Components, and Illustrative Ideas
Vision of success: Building upon and expanding USG efforts to address information integrity
and resilience globally, the U.S. Agency for International Development and U.S. Department Of
State will: 1) strengthen existing multilateral and multi-stakeholder bodies to address information
integrity; 2) improve international donor coordination; 3) enable USAID Missions to strengthen
the provision of information integrity and resilience technical assistance; and 4) integrate
diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility standards and best practices into policy making and
technical assistance. These efforts will help to strengthen private - public-civic partnerships
and develop common solutions that are coordinated and that apply lessons learned on the
most effective measures to support information integrity and resilience. This initiative will
build on the recommendations from the S4D Information Integrity Cohort's efforts and aim to
actualize one of their key recommendations to convene and scale a sustained community of
practice focused on information integrity and resilience, and coordination.
Objectives: PRO-INFO will strengthen information integrity and resilience through the
following objectives and activities:
OBJECTIVE 1: Strengthen existing multilateral / multistakeholder engagements globally to
more effectively address disinformation through increased coordination among like-minded
governments, civil society, and private sector stakeholders across the Global North and South.

PRO-INFO will deepen linkages between and across State-Department-led diplomatic
approaches at the multinational level, USAID-led development solutions at the local levels, with
a particular emphasis on the Global South. These activities will enhance collaboration and
shared understanding around key legal norms, policies and regulatory issues.
Key Components Include:
• Strengthen, Coordinate and Engage Multiple Stakeholder Fora to Expand
Capacity: increasing investments in and additional support will help to expand the
capacity of three existing multi stakeholder and multilateral bodies so that they can build
out collective solutions, strengthen coordination, and exchange lessons learned to address
information integrity and resilience globally, including in the Global South, where
information challenges are particularly acute. An effectively coordinated approach
enables the U.S. to maximize impact, strengthen partnerships, and share principles and
investments (see figure 1)
• We propose that the U.S., led by the Department of State, join the new
Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD)'s "Mis/Dis
Resource Hub." Illustrative activities for this Hub could include: create a data
hub that includes governance policies and initiatives to address information
integrity and resilience; convene a government and multi stakeholder dialogue,
build an analytical center to create consensus around effective practices; engage
with civil society, private sector, and media experts to address policy
effectiveness; and create a stocktaking review of existing development. (See Tab
1 for more details on these activities).
In addition, with State and White House active participation, PRO-INFO would
deepen cooperation and engagement with other multilateral bodies that address
information integrity and resilience, most notably, the G7 Rapid Response
Mechanism (G7 RRM) and U.S.- EU Trade and Technology Council (TTC). This
will enable us

OBJECTIVE 2: Build on and expand donor coordination to support information integrity
and resilience.

USAID will encourage donor agencies and the private sector to increase and more effectively
allocate resources. Across this objective, USAID will help shape donor priorities through policy
dialogues and by identifying country-level lessons learned.
• Harmonize Approaches Across Governments: This activity will rally like-minded
governments and philanthropies to invest and fund activities to strengthen information
integrity and resilience, most notably in the Global South. USAID will seek to boost
donor coordination efforts at the OECD (through, for example, the Development
Assistance Committee, the Mis-Dis Hub, and/or Govnet) by establishing a platform for
donor coordination on information integrity and resilience, as described in the following
paragraph below. In addition, it will strengthen coordination within other multilateral
bodies that the U.S. participates in with donors, including the European Union and G7
countries.
• Ensure that the Cohort on Information Integrity Endures Post S4D2: In addition to
OECD DAC and the Hub, USAID will also seek to institutionalize the Summit for
Democracy Cohort on Information Integrity in order to establish a permanent platform
for coordination to address MDM. The body could be housed under a multilateral or
foundation entity and would provide a permanent home for like-minded partners who are
already actively addressing these issues-including current cohort members from like-
minded governments, civil society and foundations. Efforts would be made to expand
existing membership and to elevate the critical need for greater private sector
engagement. The Cohort would provide an important platform for members to identify
the most urgent information integrity issues, establish an order of priority for addressing
those issues, and promote greater investment of resources to tackle these priorities.
OBJECTIVE 3: Strengthen USAID's information integrity and resilience programming
through technical assistance, evidence and learning, and multi-stakeholder partnerships at the
local level.
USAID development activities complement Objectives 1 and 2 by incorporating best practices
into USAID programming. These efforts will focus on providing technical assistance and
funding to USAID partners on the ground at the regional level, as well as advancing evidence
and learning in this space.
Key Components May Include:
• Expand Effective Models, Technical Assistance, and Rapid Response Funding:
Building on successes and lessons learned from existing programs, USAID will develop a
suite of tools and services to support country level programming led by USAID Missions.
This component could include:
• Showcase "Model" Country and Regional Programs: USAID would draw
upon existing, successful USAID-supported programs, to identify and share
lessons learned and emerging practices with other USAID Missions, donors, or
civil society groups. USAID regional platforms could coordinate study tours and
regional exchanges to disseminate research as well as programmatic lessons
learned, provide technical assistance to bilateral missions, and foster private
3

sector partnerships with regional and multinational private sector entities. They
could also provide opportunities for private - public-civic partnerships at the
country level, to include partnering with local private sector entities to bring best
in class solutions to address information integrity and resilience. These include:
digital platforms, as appropriate, emerging technology solutions, advertising, and
strategic communications capabilities.
Expand Technical Assistance: USAID would expand technical assistance to
USAID Missions for design support or amendments to existing programming.
This would include support for comprehensive planning and design such as:
conducting local assessments and political economy analyses, drafting
contextually based program design and procurement documents, supporting
technical evaluations of programs, development monitoring and evaluation
baselines and ongoing tracking, feedback support for adaptation, and work
planning.
Provide advanced support for Localization, Adaptation and Scaling: USAID
would assist staff or local partners to co-create local adaptation of model
programs, and source the appropriate technical assistance needed for the
adaptation or new programming. Rapid Response support through this initiative
could fund small, innovative pilots to kick-start programs to address information
integrity and resilience for priority missions, and local civil society and private
sector partners.
• Strengthen Evidence and Learning: While USAID and partners have sourced key
lessons learned, it is important to improve evidence-based understanding of how MDM
affects and undermines USAID's democracy and human rights efforts, as well as the
efforts of other development sectors. Given the current disconnect between research and
practice, these activities will build consensus around a learning agenda, indicators of
measurement, and theories of change. USAID will build upon its global experience in
programming in the information integrity and resilience space to generate applied
learning products for dissemination among the development community. The following
resources and tools will be developed within USAID and can be shared with the OECD
Mis/Dis Resource Hub, G7 RRM, and the TTC for broader uptake and coordination.
This component will produce:
MDM Research Best Practices Guidebook: Building from the 2021 USAID
Disinformation/Misinformation primer and the assessment of current
programming, this guidebook will recommend a detailed set of approaches,
including analytic frameworks for data collection and aggregate information
integrity and resilience performance indicators. The guidebook will address a
range of operating contexts and program characteristics that will assist policy and
programming specialists in adapting methods in new contexts.
MDM Learning Event Series: Created for the broad community of
policymakers, donors, practitioners, experts, and academics to inform
programmatic effectiveness.
Learning Tools: To address the dynamic growth of knowledge about
mis/disinformation, we will continuously produce a range of accessible digital
content such as an update of the 2021 USAID Disinformation Primer, e-learning
modules, podcasts and briefs, offering continuing education and professional

development opportunities to advance understanding of MDM issues, tactics, and
solutions.
OBJECTIVE 4: Integrate Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEIA) into
MDM programming. Information integrity programming must consider the impact of
mis/disinformation on all members of society and to build an information ecosystem that ensures
trust and safety for numerous publics. Women, LGBTI+, minority communities, and
marginalized communities are disproportionately affected by disinformation: frequently targeted
and victimized by it. The guiding principle of this initiative will address how these groups are
affected by MDM and will explore how to support their leadership, representation and
participation in all aspects of the information ecosystem, research community, and policy
dialogue. Illustrative activities include:
• Convene civil society, policy makers and advocates to put forward a roadmap for the
strategies, legislation and specific tools needed to ensure policymaking and regulatory
frameworks related to the information ecosystem, including digital security acts and
media policies, are inclusive of a DEIA framework
• Capacity development and training opportunities for policymakers and advocates around
LGBTQ+, social inclusion and DEIA principles as they relate to disinformation,
misinformation and malinformation
• Offer small grants, fellowships, and mentoring opportunities for women, LGBT+ and
other minority groups to improve their knowledge, networks, and leadership skills related
to public policy and advocacy around MDM issues.
• Support measures to coordinate and collaborate with international efforts and
communities that address the gender and MDM axis.
• Include representation from historically marginalized and underrepresented community
members - inclusive of a broad representation of all stakeholders.
• Ensure indicators on evidence-based frameworks are inclusive and equitable and are
disaggregated appropriately.
• Mitigate barriers to participation/amplify voices of underrepresented communities in
advocacy platforms.

TAB 1 - Support U.S. Department of State leadership in joining the OECD "Mis/Dis
Resource Hub." The Mis/Dis Resource Hub is a new platform under the OECD that is open to
like-minded governments, including those from the Global South, practitioners, project
implementers, academics, and private sector actors, the initiative will foster knowledge sharing
on-the-ground as well as within global forums to build understanding of the most effective
measures and increase coordination for their implementation to strengthen societies ability to
address information integrity and resilience. USAID will support State Department colleagues
in joining the OECD initiative to expand this platform to focus on the institutional and policy
solutions, including whole-of-society partnerships, that are required to fight mis- and dis-
information and strengthen information ecosystems. The "Hub" will engage OECD's
membership and multi-disciplinary directorates, committees, and the DAC to create formal and
enduring channels to engage with civil society and private sector, identify effective approaches,
priorities, and supporting coordination of implementation. The "Hub" will provide:
• A data hub that includes governance policies and initiatives to address information
integrity and resilience. Building on the collective experiences of OECD member
countries by serving as an archive for relevant documents and resources, to include
governance policies and initiatives aimed at preparing for and responding to the
publication and spread of mis- and dis-information, as well as regulatory and policy
measures designed to increase transparency and prevention, and reduce the economic and
structural drivers behind mis- and dis-information. It will compare state approaches,
expand the knowledge of key actors, partnerships, and measures to address
disinformation to support reactions to real-time evolutions of emerging threats and
prepare for future challenges.
• A convener of government and multi stakeholder dialogue. The "Hub" will convene
regular government and multi stakeholder dialogue via the informal OECD Expert Group
on Preventing and Combating Mis- and Dis-information, which includes experts and
practitioners from across governments and will draw on efforts of other related OECD
committees. The Hub will invite relevant experts from the private sector and civil society,
including stakeholders from the Global South to participate in the multi stakeholder
dialogue.
• An analytical center. Based on the convenings, data collected, and surveys, the "Hub"
will develop a Report on Public Governance Responses to strengthen information
integrity and resilience to advance policy making and build consensus around effective
practices within the context of broader efforts to reinforce democracy. The report will
support the design of governance measures to address threats and build more resilient
societies; policy measures related to social media platform transparency and prevention
measures; and policy measures that reduce economic and structural drivers of the spread
of disinformation. It will identify innovative mechanisms for effective co-operation of
governments, the media and civil society organizations and inform the understanding of
good practices regarding whole-of-government and whole-of- society approaches to
tackling disinformation and strengthening media and information ecosystems.
• A forum for engagement with civil society, private sector, and media experts to
address policy effectiveness. This will include data collection and analysis to bring
greater clarity to the "policy effectiveness" question, and support OECD's membership in
developing approaches to countering disinformation that are informed by the success and

"Hub" will partner with the Forum on Information and Democracy and other relevant

perspectives inform the global reflection on the relevant challenges and governance
responses.
• Taxonomy of Approaches: a stocktaking review of existing development programming
designed to strengthen information integrity and resilience and development of a
classification system of program types and theories of change.
